title: Pasta alla Norcina
subtitle: Sausage, white wine & cream · about 30 minutes
description: A rich Umbrian pasta with browned Italian sausage, white wine and double cream, finished with pecorino Romano.

steps.text: Remove the casings from the {{sausages}} and break the meat apart. Add to a cold pan with a little {{oil}} and set to medium-high. Brown until crispy and golden with the fat rendered.
Crack in {{pepper}}, then add the {{fennel}} and {{garlic}}. Cook until fragrant.
Pour in the {{wine}} and scrape the base of the pan to lift the caramelised bits. Reduce until almost gone.
Add the {{cream}} and lower to a gentle bubbling simmer.
Cook the {{pasta}} in boiling water salted with {{salt}} until al dente.
Taste the sauce and adjust seasoning. Add the pasta with a ladle or two of pasta water and let it finish cooking in the sauce.
Lower the heat, sprinkle over the {{pecorino}} with a splash more pasta water, and mix vigorously until melted and creamy. Loosen with more pasta water or tighten with more cheese as needed.
Plate up and top with extra black pepper and pecorino Romano.

notes: The original didn't specify a pasta amount — 100g dried pasta per person is used here.
Save a mug of starchy pasta water before draining; it's what pulls the sauce together.
If your sausages are already well seasoned, you can skip the added fennel.

nutrition.note: Approximate, per serving at 4 servings. Estimated from typical ingredient values — actual figures vary with the sausages, cream and pasta you use.
